title: Can AI widen loan review coverage without losing independence?
description: AI loan review and credit risk monitoring for community banks and credit unions: what it flags, who signs, current exam guidance and failed-bank lessons.
topic: AI loan review and credit risk monitoring
verdict: Loan review independently checks loan grades. Vendors say AI can read every file between reviews and flag the gaps[^1][^48].
No rule sets a minimum share for your own loan review. Even FDIC examiners use no fixed ratio[^1][^4].
In our read of nine failed-bank reviews, five showed loan-book problems; insiders altered records in two[^29][^34].
Reviewers keep the grade and the sign-off. AI drafts with page citations, and a person validates each line[^16][^17].
Test on last year's downgrades first: language models still miss numbers on multi-document financial work[^24][^26].

summary: Loan review is the independent check that loans are graded right and problems surface early[^1][^2]. Vendors report AI that reads every commercial file between reviews, drafts the reviewer's write-up with page citations and flags grade gaps[^17][^46][^48]. Clean core data and reviewers independent of lending make or break it[^2][^4].
humanRole: Loan reviewer: checks every AI flag and draft against the cited pages before it enters the official file[^17]. At Old National, AI output is not examiner-visible, and reviewers validate it (Abrigo case, vendor-reported, 2026)[^16].

Loan review stays independent of lending: reviewers don't originate the loans and aren't paid on the ratings[^1]. Keep the AI's prompts, thresholds and flag list with loan review, not lenders, to protect that independence[^1].
Chief credit officer: settles lender-versus-reviewer grade disputes through an appeal process, which the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) expects[^2].
Board: approves the loan review policy each year and receives the findings, typically every quarter[^1][^2].
teamAfter: Reviewers move from reading every page to checking flagged and larger credits. Teams on automated software report 4.6 files per reviewer a week, against 3.6 manual (Abrigo survey, vendor)[^18].
Watch-list loans get borrower calls and site visits, since soft information is where AI helps least[^21][^28].

Reviewers spend more time on trends for the board and the allowance for credit losses (ACL)[^1]. Seacoast aims to automate every nonjudgmental part of credit risk review by 2028 (Abrigo case, vendor-reported)[^17].
Headcount isn't the goal: of firms using AI, 66% only use it to help staff, and only 2% of firms report AI-related job losses[^20].

example.input: Illustrative: a $900M community bank with two loan reviewers and an outsourced annual review that samples the largest loans and a slice of the rest[^1]. Each month the AI gets the commercial trial balance with grades, core payment history, extension and overdraft reports, statements and covenant certificates[^1].
example.output: A ranked flag list with page citations: loan 4471, graded pass, shows debt service coverage down from 1.35x to 0.98x against a 1.20x covenant[^17]. The reviewer opens the cited pages, agrees or rejects, and records why[^16]. Grade changes go to the chief credit officer and the lender appeal step[^2].

recipes.name: 1. Small team already on loan review software
recipes.when: One to three reviewers, often at a $250M to $1B bank, already on a loan review platform with an AI module. Abrigo reports Old National and Seacoast use one with human validation (vendor-reported, 2026)[^15][^17].
flow: Loan review officer: switch on the AI module and choose what it drafts
Credit admin: load the trial balance, statements and covenant certificates
AI: draft each line sheet, the reviewer's write-up of one loan, with page citations
Reviewer: check each line against the cited pages, then accept or reject
Chief credit officer: sign grade changes after the lender appeal step
Loan review officer: report findings to the board each quarter
recipes.cost: Most AI modules carry no published price, so expect a vendor quote[^19][^46]. The lowest published loan review software price is LenderAnalyzer's, from $99 a month, read 26 Nov 2026[^45].

recipes.name: 2. Mid-size bank with a covenant-heavy commercial book
recipes.when: A $1B to $5B bank, heavy in commercial real estate (CRE), whose loan platform already tracks covenants and statement dates. Interagency guidance lets key risk indicators set how often and how deeply you review[^1].
flow: Credit admin: map covenants and statement due dates in the platform
AI: test covenants and flag deteriorating credits every month
Loan review: review flagged loans first, then the usual scope list
Lender: answer each flag in writing
Chief credit officer: approve or reject grade changes
Loan review officer: log every rating change, a risk indicator OCC examiners track
recipes.cost: Monitoring modules from nCino and Moody's publish no price, so cost comes from a quote[^46][^47]. As a floor, published loan review software starts from $99 a month, read 26 Nov 2026[^45].

recipes.name: 3. Your own rules on core data, with an analyst
recipes.when: A bank or credit union with a data analyst and core extracts, often next to an outsourced annual review. Fixed rules fall outside SR 26-2's definition of a model[^49].
flow: Data analyst: pull payments, extensions, overdrafts, maturity changes and statement dates from the core
Rules: flag stale financials, repeated extensions, overdrafts and maturity changes with no renewal memo
Reviewer: triage the list and pull the files
Internal audit: reconcile a sample of core fields to loan documents
Risk management: document the rules and the test results
recipes.cost: We found no public cost figure for an in-house build, so price it as analyst time on tools you own. For scale, published loan review software starts from $99 a month, read 26 Nov 2026[^45].

rules.name: Interagency Guidance on Credit Risk Review Systems (2020)
rules.status: In force at the Federal Reserve, Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC), OCC and National Credit Union Administration (NCUA)
rules.what: Loan review must be independent of lending, follow a board-approved policy and report to the board[^1]. Key risk indicators may set how often and how deeply loans are reviewed[^1]. Credit risk review is not internal audit[^1].

rules.name: OCC booklet, Lending and Loan Portfolio Risk Management (June 2026)
rules.status: In force; it rescinded the 1998 Loan Portfolio Management booklet
rules.what: Examiners check review frequency, scope, delayed reviews, board reports and the rating appeal process[^2][^3]. Lending models belong under model risk management[^2].

rules.name: OCC booklet, Rating Credit Risk (2001)
rules.what: Every credit is formally reviewed at least once a year, and rating systems are back-tested[^13]. Some large banks use credit models to confirm and supplement judgmentally assigned ratings[^13].

rules.name: FDIC Risk Management Manual, Section 3.2 Loans
rules.what: Lists what a loan review policy should cover[^4]. FDIC examiners use no minimum or maximum loan penetration ratio when they sample loans[^4].

rules.name: NCUA rule, 12 CFR 723.4
rules.what: Credit unions with commercial loans need periodic loan review, a risk rating system and an exceptions process[^6].

rules.name: SR 26-2, model risk management (17 Apr 2026)
rules.status: In force; it replaced SR 11-7 and SR 21-8
rules.what: SR 26-2 replaced SR 11-7 and SR 21-8, and is most relevant to banks over $30B[^7]. The guidance leaves generative and agentic AI out of scope and excludes fixed rules[^49]. Banks stay responsible for models they buy from vendors[^49].

rules.name: OCC Bulletin 2026-54, Super Intelligence (AI) supervisory framework
rules.what: The OCC now uses the term super intelligence (SI) for AI, treats it as no separate risk category and adds no new expectations[^8]. Controls scale with consequences and the degree of human oversight[^8].

rules.name: Interagency third-party guidance, FDIC FIL-29-2023
rules.status: In force; a September 2026 proposal would replace it, comments due 16 Dec 2026
rules.what: An AI vendor or outsourced reviewer is a third party, and the bank stays responsible for the work[^10][^11]. Proposed guidance (FIL-58-2026) would replace it once final[^11][^12].

rules.name: NCUA AI resources
rules.what: The NCUA supervises AI like any other new technology, focusing on risk management, not the tool[^9].

howToTest: Record today's numbers: files per reviewer a week, commercial dollars covered, grade changes per review and exam findings. Surveyed teams average 3.6 files a week manual, 4.6 automated (vendor survey)[^18].
Build a test set from last year's closed reviews, with every downgrade and every loan examiners graded lower. Examiner-versus-management gaps were the warning sign at Metropolitan Capital[^37].
Run the AI blind on that set and compare its flags with the final grades. Count missed downgrades first, then false flags.
Check every number it quotes against the source page. The best model scored 82.4% on financial spreadsheets, and complex synthesis averaged 0.31[^24][^25].
Check the grades it suggests against how those loans actually performed, as the OCC expects of any rating system[^13].
Run one review cycle in parallel: reviewers do their normal sample while AI reads every loan. Keep AI output out of the official file until a reviewer validates it[^16][^17].
Pilot one segment first, such as commercial real estate, and widen to the whole book only after a clean parallel cycle.
Test the data feed, not just the model: reconcile maturity dates and past-due status to loan documents. The OCC found Lindsay's CEO altered exactly those core fields[^34].
Price the lift: reviewer hours freed times loaded cost, plus commercial dollars newly reviewed. Old National's 15-40% gain by review type is a vendor-reported reference only[^15].
Document it for examiners: list the tool with your lending models and third parties, plus the validation results[^2].
watchOuts: Optimistic grades go unchallenged: Metropolitan Capital's management routinely applied unreasonable risk scores[^37]. Compare each grade to its numbers and send gaps to loan review, not the lender.
Extensions and deferrals hide trouble: examiners cited liberal deferrals and extensions, and weak loan review, at Community Bank & Trust[^38]. Flag repeated extensions as a trigger.
The records themselves can be wrong: the OCC found Lindsay's CEO changed maturity dates and past-due status in the core[^34][^33]. Reconcile core fields to signed loan documents.
Independence leaks if lenders tune the tool[^1][^4]. Loan review should own the prompts, thresholds and flag list.
Confident wrong numbers: accuracy falls 18.60% on multi-period work[^26]. Require page citations and recompute ratios with fixed formulas.

Capacity mistaken for quality: more files per reviewer is not a better catch rate, as Abrigo's own survey warns[^18]. Measure the catch rate on downgrades, and treat vendor speed claims as claims[^18].

faq.q: How much of the loan portfolio should loan review cover?
faq.a: No regulator sets a fixed minimum share for your own review, though Fed examiners sample at least 10% at $10B to $100B state member banks[^1][^14]. The FDIC tells its examiners the right loans in the sample matter more than the percentage[^4]. The Fed expects internal review to cover substantially more than the examiners' sample[^14].

faq.q: How often should loans be reviewed?
faq.a: Significant loans are typically reviewed once a year, at renewal, or more often when risk rises[^1][^5]. Key risk indicators can raise or lower that frequency[^1].

faq.q: Can a small bank or credit union do loan review in-house?
faq.a: Yes, if reviewers are independent of origination and not paid on the ratings, or you use a qualified third party[^1]. Credit unions generally use third-party reviewers[^42].

faq.q: Will examiners accept AI-assisted loan review?
faq.a: Yes, if reviewers stay in charge: the OCC's November 2026 framework sets no new expectations, and the NCUA treats AI like any other technology[^8][^9]. Keep reviewer sign-off and validation records[^16].

faq.q: Is AI loan review a model under model risk management?
faq.a: Only partly, because SR 26-2, which replaced SR 11-7, leaves generative AI out of scope and excludes fixed rules[^7][^49]. The OCC still expects lending models under model risk management[^2].

faq.q: What's the difference between loan review and internal audit?
faq.a: Loan review grades credit risk, while internal audit tests whether controls work, loan review included[^1]. The guidance keeps the two functions separate[^1].

buyVsBuild.buy: Buy the file reading and line-sheet drafting: 76% of enterprise AI solutions were bought in 2025, up from 53%[^43]. Bought or partnered pilots reached deployment about twice as often as internal builds[^44]. Loan review platforms already ship document AI[^17][^19].
buyVsBuild.build: Build the flags that run on your own core data, where the rules are yours and easy to explain[^49]. Fixed rules sit outside SR 26-2's model definition, and 84% of small banks have never posted an AI job, so keep the build simple[^49][^21].

pickElse: Mostly consumer or small, similar loans: track delinquency by loan type and by the year loans were made, in your core or allowance software. One Community Development Financial Institutions (CDFI) Fund memo suggests 10-15% sampling for similar products[^41].

A few hundred commercial loans and one reviewer: a covenant reminder report and a stale-financials report may be enough. Low-cost loan review software starts from $99 a month (vendor price, read 26 Nov 2026)[^45].
Core data you can't trust: fix the data first, with a reconciliation project that internal audit tests. Altered core fields hid Lindsay's bad loans[^34].
You need an independent annual opinion for the board or examiners: keep an independent reviewer, in-house or outsourced, and let AI support them[^1].

answers.human-role: Your reviewers stay in charge: AI drafts and flags, reviewers validate each line, the chief credit officer settles grade disputes and the board approves policy[^1][^2][^16].
answers.team-after: Reviewers move from reading every page to checking flagged and larger credits, visiting watch-list borrowers and reporting trends to the board[^18][^21][^1].
answers.example: Core data and loan files go in, and a ranked flag list with page citations comes out for a reviewer to accept or reject[^17][^1].
answers.table-1: Several loan review and monitoring tools now draft line sheets, test covenants and suggest grades, vendors say, and only one publishes a price, from $99 a month[^17][^47][^48][^45].
answers.table-2: Most loan review teams are exploring AI, but under a quarter use it: 74.4% use, explore or plan it, and 23.1% already do[^18][^22].
answers.table-3: AI is accurate enough to draft and flag, not to grade alone: the best model scored 82.4% on financial spreadsheets, about one error in six[^24][^25].
answers.recipes: Start with an add-on if you run loan review software, platform monitoring if it holds your covenants, or your own rules if you have core data and an analyst[^15][^47][^49].
answers.own-data: Five of the nine failed-bank reviews we read found loan-book problems a file or core-data check could flag, and in two of those, insiders altered records[^29][^34].
answers.rules: The 2020 interagency credit risk review guidance sets the base, with the OCC's June 2026 booklet, FDIC and NCUA manuals, and SR 26-2 for models[^1][^2][^7].
answers.benchmark: Run the AI blind on last year's closed reviews, count missed downgrades, check its numbers against source pages, then run one cycle in parallel[^18][^37][^16].
answers.what-goes-wrong: AI loan review goes wrong when optimistic grades go unchallenged, extensions hide trouble, core records are altered, lenders tune the tool, or numbers come out confidently wrong[^37][^38][^34].
answers.buy-or-build: Buy the file reading and line-sheet drafting, and build the core-data flags that loan review owns[^43][^49].
answers.something-else: Pick something else when your book is mostly consumer loans, you have one reviewer, your core data is unreliable, or you need an independent annual opinion[^41][^45][^34].

offer.heading: Which loans would your review flag this month? Get a free diagnostic
offer.body: Bring a recent trial balance and your loan review policy. In 30 minutes we map, on your own book, where AI can widen coverage and where your reviewers stay in charge. You leave with the first step and a before-and-after measure, in writing, with no sales pitch.

reviews.notes: Could tell in seconds what the page answers. The example had no 'before', so the input now says the annual review samples the largest loans and a slice of the rest. On this page had no route to the build options; added a link to the three recipes.

Tripped on 'line sheet', 'hold-out set', 'back-test', 'covenant tickler', 'vintages' and bare OCC, FDIC, NCUA and CSBS. Line sheet is now 'the reviewer's write-up of one loan'; the test steps say 'test set' and 'check suggested grades against how loans performed'; pick-else lines use plain words; each regulator and CSBS is spelled out on first use.

Wanted to know whether one part of the book can pilot first. Added a test step: pilot one segment, such as commercial real estate, and widen only after a clean parallel cycle. The price-the-lift step already counts reviewer hours freed and dollars newly reviewed.

Chief credit officer checked the rules. Every model-risk mention names SR 26-2 as the replacement for SR 11-7 and FIL-27-2021; the 1998 OCC booklet appears only as rescinded; FIL-29-2023 shows the Sep 2026 replacement proposal (comments due 16 Dec 2026, checked on fdic.gov). SR 14-4's examiner sample now reads $10B to $100B, per the revised Fed letter. Added that banks stay responsible for vendor models, and footnoted 'credit risk review is not internal audit'. Independence of loan review from lending is explicit in human role and watch-outs.

Liked the plain cost line: vendors publish no price, with one labelled $99-a-month floor, and no consulting fees anywhere. The vendor bank results are labelled as vendor-reported with the year. No sourced pilot timeline exists, so none is promised. The offer now says the diagnostic maps his own book, with a first step and a before-and-after measure in writing.
